patch_description: Instead of optimizing all 26 free coordinates with soft-min gradients (which gets stuck in poor local minima from random starts), this approach exploits the strong empirical evidence that optimal Heilbronn configurations for n=13 exhibit 3-fold rotational symmetry. The configuration is parametrized as: one point at the center (the only fixed point of a 120° rotation) plus 4 "orbits" of 3 points each generated by rotating 4 base points by 0°, 120°, 240°. This reduces the search from 26 dimensions to just 8, making coordinate-descent hill climbing (with adaptive shrinking steps) extremely effective and fast. A final short symmetry-breaking polish on all 26 coordinates squeezes out extra area. The tiny search space means many deterministic seeds can be exhausted in well under a second, reliably beating the benchmark score of ~0.0309.
